**Item 6.2 – Application P2024/0891 – Warehouse and Cold Storage Facility, 14 Mason St, Altona North**

**Applicant:** Freshlink Cold Chain Logistics Pty Ltd

**Proposal:** Construction of a warehouse and cold storage facility, including a 12 metre high building, refrigeration plant, 24/7 operation, and associated car parking and loading areas.

**Previous Consideration:** The application was referred to the Planning Committee following the conclusion of the public notice period and the preparation of the officer assessment report (dated 28 May 2025). The report had recommended approval subject to conditions.

**Officer Presentation:**

Senior Planner K. Patel presented the report. He provided an overview of the site context, noting the subject land is located within the Industrial 1 Zone and is adjacent to residential properties to the east. Mr Patel summarised the key elements of the proposal, including the total floor area of approximately 4,850sqm, the proposed hours of operation (24 hours, 7 days per week), and the number of loading docks (six).

Mr Patel noted that the application was advertised in accordance with Section 52 of the Planning and Environment Act 1987. A total of 14 objections were received during the public notice period. The key issues raised in the objections were summarised in the report and included traffic, noise, hours of operation, visual amenity, property values, and cumulative impacts.

Mr Patel advised that the applicant had provided a revised traffic impact assessment (dated 2 June 2025) and an amended acoustic report (dated 4 June 2025) in response to concerns raised by Council's traffic engineers and the objectors. These amended reports addressed a number of the issues raised, including the provision of a swept path analysis for the larger articulated vehicles and the incorporation of a high-performance acoustic barrier along the eastern boundary.

**Discussion:**

Cr Delaney queried the adequacy of the amended acoustic report, specifically whether the night time noise levels had been reassessed. Mr Patel advised that the amended report included additional night time noise monitoring undertaken between 10pm and 6am over a three night period. The amended report concluded that with the recommended conditions (including the upgraded acoustic fence and restrictions on reversing beepers during night time hours), the proposal would meet the relevant State Environment Protection Policy (Control of Noise from Commerce, Industry and Trade) requirements.

Cr Tse asked about the traffic conditions. Mr Patel advised that the amended traffic assessment recommended a number of conditions, including the requirement for all trucks to enter and exit the site in a forward direction, a restriction on truck movements during the peak hour (7-9am and 4-6pm) except for light commercial vehicles, and the provision of a truck waiting area on site to prevent queuing on Mason St.

Cr Whitfield raised a concern regarding the cumulative impact of the development, noting that several objectors had raised this issue. Mr Patel advised that while the planning scheme does not require a cumulative impact assessment for an application of this nature, the traffic and acoustic assessments had taken into account the existing background levels in the area. The amended traffic assessment had also modelled the additional traffic generated by the proposal in conjunction with the existing traffic volumes on Mason St.

The subject site is an irregular-shaped lot of 2.14 hectares, located on the north side of Mason St, approximately 300 m east of the intersection with Grieve Pde. The site is currently developed with:

**5. SUBMISSIONS RECEIVED**

Pursuant to section 57 of the Planning and Environment Act 1987, the application was advertised by mail to adjoining and nearby owners and occupiers, and by a sign on the site. The public notice period ran from 20 November 2024 to 10 January 2025 inclusive, taking into account the extended advertising period over the Christmas shutdown.

A total of 14 submissions were received during the notice period. Of these, 12 were objections and 2 were letters of support. A summary of the key issues raised is provided below.

**5.1 Objections Received**

The majority of objections were received from residents of the residential streets immediately to the east of the site, particularly those in Fawker St and Grieve Pde. A coordinated objection campaign appears to have been undertaken by the Altona North Community Action Group, with several submissions containing near-identical wording. The key concerns raised in the objections are summarised as follows:

- **Traffic and access**: Concern that the proposed increase in heavy vehicle movements (up to 40 per day at peak) will exacerbate existing congestion at the intersection of Mason St and Blackshaws Rd. Objectors noted that this intersection already operates at capacity during peak periods and that the proposed development does not include any upgrade works to this intersection. One submission (Objection 3) stated "the trucks will be queing down Mason St and blocking the driveways of existing businesses". Another objector (Objection 7) noted that the existing businesses in Mason St already generate significant truck movements and that the cumulative impact has not been properly assessed.

- **Noise**: Concerns regarding noise from the refrigeration plant, truck movements during night time hours, and the use of reversing beepers. Several objectors noted that the site is in close proximity to residential dwellings to the east, and that the existing acoustic fence along the eastern boundary is in poor condition. Objection 5 queried whether the noise assessment had measured background noise levels during the night time period, stating "I dont believe the noise report reflects the quiet of the night time in this area".

- **Hours of operation**: Objectors raised concern that the proposed 24/7 operation would result in noise and traffic impacts during the night time period, contrary to the existing residential amenity. Some objectors noted that the site currently operates on a limited basis and that the use of the existing cold storage facility is not comparable to the proposed intensity of use.

- **Visual amenity and built form**: Concern that the proposed 12 metre high building would be visually dominant when viewed from the residential area to the east. Objection 11 noted that the "building will tower over the existing houses and the roof top plant will be an eyesore".

- **Property values**: A small number of objectors raised concern that the development would have a negative impact on property values in the area. No substantive evidence was provided in support of these claims.

- **Cumulative impacts**: Several objectors noted that the site is located within an established industrial area that is undergoing significant change, and that the cumulative impact of multiple developments in the area has not been assessed. These concerns are noted, however the planning scheme does not require a cumulative impact assessment for an application of this nature.

**Item 6.2 – Application P2024/0891 – Warehouse and Cold Storage Facility, 14 Mason St, Altona North**

**Applicant:** Freshlink Cold Chain Logistics Pty Ltd

**Proposal:** Construction of a warehouse and cold storage facility, including a 12 metre high building, refrigeration plant, 24/7 operation, and associated car parking and loading areas.

**Previous Consideration:** The application was referred to the Planning Committee following the conclusion of the public notice period and the preparation of the officer assessment report (dated 28 May 2025). The report had recommended approval subject to conditions.

**Officer Presentation:**

Senior Planner K. Patel presented the report. He provided an overview of the site context, noting the subject land is located within the Industrial 1 Zone and is adjacent to residential properties to the east. Mr Patel summarised the key elements of the proposal, including the total floor area of approximately 4,850sqm, the proposed hours of operation (24 hours, 7 days per week), and the number of loading docks (six).

Mr Patel noted that the application was advertised in accordance with Section 52 of the Planning and Environment Act 1987. A total of 14 objections were received during the public notice period. The key issues raised in the objections were summarised in the report and included traffic, noise, hours of operation, visual amenity, property values, and cumulative impacts.

Mr Patel advised that the applicant had provided a revised traffic impact assessment (dated 2 June 2025) and an amended acoustic report (dated 4 June 2025) in response to concerns raised by Council's traffic engineers and the objectors. These amended reports addressed a number of the issues raised, including the provision of a swept path analysis for the larger articulated vehicles and the incorporation of a high-performance acoustic barrier along the eastern boundary.

**Discussion:**

Cr Delaney queried the adequacy of the amended acoustic report, specifically whether the night time noise levels had been reassessed. Mr Patel advised that the amended report included additional night time noise monitoring undertaken between 10pm and 6am over a three night period. The amended report concluded that with the recommended conditions (including the upgraded acoustic fence and restrictions on reversing beepers during night time hours), the proposal would meet the relevant State Environment Protection Policy (Control of Noise from Commerce, Industry and Trade) requirements.

Cr Tse asked about the traffic conditions. Mr Patel advised that the amended traffic assessment recommended a number of conditions, including the requirement for all trucks to enter and exit the site in a forward direction, a restriction on truck movements during the peak hour (7-9am and 4-6pm) except for light commercial vehicles, and the provision of a truck waiting area on site to prevent queuing on Mason St.

Cr Whitfield raised a concern regarding the cumulative impact of the development, noting that several objectors had raised this issue. Mr Patel advised that while the planning scheme does not require a cumulative impact assessment for an application of this nature, the traffic and acoustic assessments had taken into account the existing background levels in the area. The amended traffic assessment had also modelled the additional traffic generated by the proposal in conjunction with the existing traffic volumes on Mason St.

**Grounds of Appeal (summary as lodged):**
1. The permit conditions do not adequately protect residential amenity with respect to noise, particularly the operation of mechanical plant and refrigeration units.
2. The acoustic assessment relied upon by Council did not model the cumulative effect of the proposed plant alongside existing industrial uses in the area.
3. The condition restricting reversing beepers between 10pm and 6am is insufficient and unenforceable in practice.
